content.text:
**Finding: compliant** (rule LD — liquidated damages/penalties payable by Customer).

The agreement is silent on Customer-payable stipulated amounts:

- **§ 3 (Compensation)** — time-and-materials fees, out-of-pocket expenses and taxes only; no late-payment interest, penalty or forfeiture mechanic.
- **§ 6 (Termination)** and the duplicate **§ 7(c)** — on termination for convenience or for cause, Contractor is paid only "all fees and expenses that have been incurred or earned … through the effective date of such termination." That is accrued consideration, not an early-termination fee or minimum commitment.
- **§ 7(a)–(b)** — mutual liability caps and consequential damages waiver; no stipulated-damages language in either direction.
- Text searches for "liquidated damages", "penalty", "stipulated", "minimum" and "forfeit" returned no hits.

This sits at the **preferred** position, so no redline was proposed.

**Finding: compliant** — no redline proposed.

The MINCOMMIT rule is satisfied at the **preferred** position, not merely the fallback:

- **§ 3(a)** — compensation is strictly **time-and-materials** per Statement of Work, i.e. fees for ordered services only.
- **§ 1(a)** — Contractor is retained **"on a task by task basis,"** with scope arising only from mutually agreed SOWs.
- **§ 6(a)** — either party may terminate **for any or no reason on 15 days' notice** when no SOW is outstanding, so there is no lock-in even in principle.

A full-text search for *minimum, commit, shortfall, retainer, take or pay, volume* returned only unrelated hits (exclusive-property/licence language in § 4 and the entire-agreement clause in § 7). No commitment exists that would need reducing or true-up treatment.

One item flagged in the rationale for context but deliberately **not** treated as a deviation here: § 3(b) allows Contractor to change rates on 30 days' notice with no cap. That is a price-escalation concern rather than a volume commitment, and raising it under MINCOMMIT would double-count a term properly owned by a price-increase rule.

paragraphs.text: 7. LIMITATIONS OF LIABILITY; INDEMNIFICATION OF CONTRACTOR.

(a) EXCEPT WITH RESPECT TO CONTRACTOR'S OBLIGATIONS PURSUANT TO PARAGRAPH 9 HEREOF, CONTRACTOR'S MAXIMUM LIABILITY TO COMPANY ARISING FOR ANY REASON RELATING TO CONTRACTOR'S PERFORMANCE OF SERVICES UNDER A STATEMENT OF WORK SHALL BE LIMITED TO THE AMOUNT OF FEES PAID TO CONTRACTOR FOR THE PERFORMANCE OF SUCH SERVICES. COMPANYS' MAXIMUM LIABILITY TO CONTRACTOR FOR ANY REASON ARISING OUT OF THIS AGREEMENT SHALL BE LIMITED TO THE AMOUNT OF FEES PAID TO CONTRACTOR.

(b) NEITHER PARTY SHALL HAVE ANY LIABILITY TO THE OTHER PARTY FOR ANY LOST PROFITS OR SPECIAL, INCIDENTAL, INDIRECT OR CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGES, EVEN IF SUCH PARTY HAS BEEN ADVISED OF THE POSSIBILITY OF SUCH DAMAGES.
(c) IN ANY SUIT ARISING FROM THIS AGREEMENT EACH PARTY SHALL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR ITS OWN ATTORNEYS FEES. COMPANY AND CONTRACTOR HEREBY WAIVE ANY CLAIM TO AWARD OF ATTORNEYS FEES IN SUCH A SUIT.

8. CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION. "Confidential Information" means all documents, software, reports, data, records, forms, conversations and other materials obtained by Contractor from Company in the course of performing any Services (including, but not limited to, Company records and information). Notwithstanding the foregoing, Confidential Information does not include information which:
(i) is or becomes publicly known through no wrongful act of Contractor; or (ii) is independently developed by Contractor without benefit of Company's

Confidential Information. Contractor shall not use or disclose to any person, firm or entity any Confidential Information without Company's express, prior written permission; provided, however, that notwithstanding the foregoing, Contractor may disclose Confidential Information to the extent that it is required to be disclosed pursuant to a statutory or regulatory provision or court order.

9. INDEPENDENT CONTRACTOR. Contractor is performing the Services as an independent contractor and not as an employee of Company and none of Contractor's personnel shall be entitled to receive any compensation, benefits or other incidents of employment from Company. Subject to Section 3(c), Contractor shall be responsible for all taxes and other expenses arising from the employment or independent contractor relationship between Contractor and its personnel and the rendition of Services hereunder by such personnel to Company. Nothing in this Agreement shall be deemed to constitute a partnership or joint venture between Company and Contractor, nor shall anything in this Agreement be deemed to constitute Contractor or Company the agent of the other. Neither Contractor nor Company shall be or become liable or bound by any representation, act or omission whatsoever of the other.

10. NONASSIGNABILITY. Neither party shall assign, transfer, or subcontract this Agreement or any of its obligations hereunder without the other party's express, prior written consent, which will not be unreasonably withheld.

11. SEVERABILITY; GOVERNING LAW. In the event that any term or provision of this Agreement shall be held to be invalid, void or unenforceable, then the remainder of this Agreement shall not be affected, impaired or invalidated, and each such term and provision of this Agreement shall be valid and enforceable to the fullest extent permitted by law. This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the Arizona, without regard to the conflict of laws provisions thereof.

(c) In the event of termination under either section 6(a) or 6(b) of this agreement, Contractor shall be paid all fees and expenses that have been incurred or earned in connection with the performance of the Services through the effective date of such termination. Upon receipt of final payment Contractor shall provide to Company, and will assigns to Company, all right, title and interest to any Works in progress.

12. INTEGRATION. This Agreement, including The Mutual Non-Disclosure Agreement and, any Statements of Work entered into pursuant hereto, constitutes the entire agreement of the parties hereto with respect to its subject matter and supersedes all prior and contemporaneous representations, proposals, discussions, and communications, whether oral or in writing. This
Agreement may be modified only in writing and shall be enforceable in accordance with its terms when signed by each of the parties hereto.

13. NON-SOLICITATION OF EMPLOYEES. Neither party shall, during the term of this Agreement and for one (1) year after its termination, solicit for hire as an employee, consultant or otherwise any of the other party's personnel who have had direct involvement with the Services, without such other party's express written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld.

14. INSURANCE. Throughout the term of this Agreement, Contractor shall maintain workers compensation insurance in the amount required by statute, comprehensive general liability insurance with coverage of at least one million dollars ($1,000,000) and professional errors and omissions insurance for bodily injury, property damage or other losses with coverage of at least one million dollars ($1,000,000), in connection with the provision of Services by Contractor pursuant to the terms of this Agreement. At Company's request, Contractor shall provide Company with certificates or other acceptable evidence of insurance or self-insurance evidencing the above coverage and shall provide Company with prompt written notice of any material change.

15. Force Majeure. Except for payment obligations hereunder, nonperformance by either party shall be excused to the extent that performance is rendered impossible by strike, acts of God, governmental acts or restrictions, failure of suppliers, or any other reason where failure to perform is beyond the control of the nonperforming party.

16. Counterparts. This Agreement may be signed in any number of counterparts, each of which shall be an original, with the same effect as if the signatures thereto and hereto were upon the same instrument.

17. Entire Agreement. This Agreement constitutes the complete and exclusive agreement between Company and Consultant concerning the work on this project, and it supersedes all other prior agreements, proposals, and representations, whether stated orally or in writing.
18. Severability. If any provision of this Agreement is invalid, illegal, or unenforceable, the remainder of this Agreement will remain in full force and effect.

19. Arbitration. Except as otherwise specified below, all actions, disputes, claims and controversies under common law, statutory law or in equity of any type or nature whatsoever, whether arising before or after the date of this Agreement, and whether directly or indirectly
relating to:
(a) this Agreement and/or any amendments and addenda hereto, or the breach, invalidity or termination hereof;

(b) any previous or subsequent agreement between the parties; and/or (c) any other relationship, transaction or dealing between the parties (collectively the "Disputes"), will be subject to and resolved by binding arbitration pursuant to the Arbitration Rules of U.S. Arbitration & Mediation, (www.usam.com). Any award or order rendered by the arbitrator may be confirmed as a judgment or order in any state or federal court of competent jurisdiction, which includes within the federal judicial district of the residence of the party against whom such award or order was entered. IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the parties hereto have caused this Agreement to be executed by their duly authorized representatives as of the Effective Date. /s/ Michael Rockford /s/ John Marcum for RadialSpark, LLC for Clear Capital

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Clear Capital; counterparty is RadialSpark, LLC.

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

Parties: we represent Clear Capital; counterparty is RadialSpark, LLC.

Rule:
ID: INSURANCE
Title: Vendor insurance
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendors that touch our data or premises carry standard insurance.
Severity: low
Category: insurance
Position — preferred:
Commercial general liability USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate; professional (E&O) USD 2M; cyber/privacy USD 5M for vendors processing Customer Data; workers' compensation as required by law; certificates on request.

Position — fallback:
E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.
Position — walk-away:
No insurance for a vendor that processes personal data or works on our premises.
Detection guidance:
Look for an insurance clause; if absent for a services/hosting vendor, deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent Clear Capital; counterparty is RadialSpark, LLC.

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

input.quote: 14. INSURANCE. Throughout the term of this Agreement, Contractor shall maintain workers compensation insurance in the amount required by statute, comprehensive general liability insurance with coverage of at least one million dollars ($1,000,000) and professional errors and omissions insurance for bodily injury, property damage or other losses with coverage of at least one million dollars ($1,000,000), in connection with the provision of Services by Contractor pursuant to the terms of this Agreement.
input.rationale: Contrary to the planner's assumption, an insurance covenant does exist at § 7 ¶ 14 (p0048). It carries workers' compensation as required by statute, CGL of USD 1,000,000, E&O of USD 1,000,000, and certificates/evidence of insurance on Company request with notice of material change — so the general liability, workers' comp and certificate elements are satisfied, and E&O sits at the playbook fallback level (USD 1M rather than the preferred USD 2M), which we note but do not redline. The material gap is cyber/privacy liability, which the fallback requires at USD 2,000,000. Contractor plainly touches our data: Confidential Information is defined at p0038 as documents, software, reports, data and records obtained by Contractor from Company in performing Services, and p0007 contemplates Contractor personnel working at Company facilities and accessing Company computer systems. With no cyber coverage at all for a vendor that handles our data and systems, the clause fails the fallback on that term. Minimal fix: insert cyber liability (network security and privacy) coverage of USD 5,000,000, scoped to where Contractor processes Company data, leaving the remaining coverages and the existing certificate mechanic untouched; USD 2,000,000 is offered as the fallback in the comment.

input.quote: 14. INSURANCE. Throughout the term of this Agreement, Contractor shall maintain workers compensation insurance in the amount required by statute, comprehensive general liability insurance with coverage of at least one million dollars ($1,000,000) and professional errors and omissions insurance for bodily injury, property damage or other losses with coverage of at least one million dollars ($1,000,000), in connection with the provision of Services by Contractor pursuant to the terms of this Agreement.
input.rationale: Contrary to the planner's assumption, an insurance covenant does exist at § 7 ¶ 14 (p0048). It carries workers' compensation as required by statute, CGL of USD 1,000,000, E&O of USD 1,000,000, and certificates/evidence of insurance on Company request with notice of material change — so the general liability, workers' comp and certificate elements are satisfied, and E&O sits at the playbook fallback level (USD 1M rather than the preferred USD 2M), which we note but do not redline. The material gap is cyber/privacy liability, which the fallback requires at USD 2,000,000. Contractor plainly touches our data: Confidential Information is defined at p0038 as documents, software, reports, data and records obtained by Contractor from Company in performing Services, and p0007 contemplates Contractor personnel working at Company facilities and accessing Company computer systems. With no cyber coverage at all for a vendor that handles our data and systems, the clause fails the fallback on that term. Minimal fix: insert cyber liability (network security and privacy) coverage of USD 5,000,000, scoped to where Contractor processes Company data, leaving the remaining coverages and the existing certificate mechanic untouched; USD 2,000,000 is offered as the fallback in the comment.

How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.

On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.

No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.

Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).

Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.

Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

input.rationale: Section 5's express warranties cover only legal compliance, authority/rights, non-infringement and anti-bribery. You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Clear Capital; counterparty is RadialSpark, LLC.

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

**Finding submitted: deviation (low severity), § 7 ¶ 14 (p0048).**

Summary of the investigation:

- **The planner's hint was wrong.** It predicted no insurance clause existed and suggested treating the rule as "missing" with an inserted paragraph. A text search found a full insurance covenant buried as ¶ 14 inside § 7 (the limitation of liability / indemnification section), which is why it didn't surface in the section outline.
- **What the existing clause already delivers:** workers' compensation as required by statute, CGL of USD 1,000,000, E&O of USD 1,000,000, plus certificates or other evidence of insurance on request and prompt notice of material change. General liability, workers' comp and the certificate mechanic are satisfied.

I confirmed Contractor actually touches our data before flagging it: "Confidential Information" (p0038) is defined as data, records and reports obtained by Contractor from Clear Capital in performing Services, and § 1(c) (p0007) contemplates Contractor personnel working at Company facilities and accessing Company computer systems. A vendor with system access and no cyber coverage approaches the walk-away condition.
- **Redline approach:** rather than inserting a duplicate insurance paragraph (which would have created a conflicting second covenant), I made a single in-line insertion adding cyber liability at USD 5,000,000, scoped to where Contractor processes Company data, leaving the other coverages and the certificate mechanic intact. The comment offers USD 2,000,000 as the fallback.

**Finding: deviation (WARRANTY)** — submitted.

- **What's there:** Section 5 warrants only legal compliance (5(a)), authority/rights (5(b)), non-infringement (5(c)) and anti-bribery (5(d)), followed by an "in lieu of all other warranties" disclaimer (5(e)). Section 1(b) has a general workmanlike-performance covenant, and Section 4 — despite its "ACCEPTANCE" heading — contains no acceptance/rejection mechanic.
- **What's missing:** any warranty that the Services or Works conform to the Specifications/documentation, any warranty duration, and any repair/re-perform/refund remedy. That fails even the fallback (90 days software / 30 days services with remedies).
- **Redline (validated, ok:true):** new Section 5(e) warranting workmanlike performance plus 90-day conformity of the Works to the Specifications, with re-performance, repair/replacement or refund at Contractor's option; disclaimer renumbered to 5(f). No carve-out was needed because the existing disclaimer already preserves express warranties.

**Finding: missing** (medium severity) — no post-termination transition or data-return provision exists.

**What I checked:**
- **§ 6 Termination** (p0032–p0033): covers only notice periods, final payment, and assignment of Works in progress.
- **p0044**: a stray duplicate termination subsection (c) — again only payment and assignment of Works.
- **§ 4 Ownership**: allocates IP in the Works but imposes no obligation to deliver back Clear Capital's data.
- **§ 8 Confidential Information** (p0038–p0040): use and disclosure restrictions only; notably no return-or-destroy obligation on termination.

Nothing in the Agreement addresses transition assistance, data export format/timing, or deletion, so the rule fails both the preferred and fallback positions by absence.

**Redline (validated, ok:true):** inserted a new § 6(c) at the preferred position — up to six months of transition assistance at RadialSpark's then-current rates, return of Company data, Works and Confidential Information within 30 days in a commonly used machine-readable format, and deletion plus written certification thereafter. I deliberately swept in "Works and Confidential Information" alongside data, since the confidentiality clause has no return mechanic of its own and this is the natural home for one. The comment flags 90 days of assistance as an available fallback if RadialSpark pushes back on the six-month tail.

It fails the fallback on one material term, however: there is no carve-out for general advertisements or unsolicited approaches, which the rule summary treats as a condition of acceptability (\"only narrow, time-limited non-solicits with a general-advertising carve-out\"). We therefore propose the minimal fallback edit — a single carve-out sentence for untargeted solicitations and unsolicited approaches — rather than the preferred position (no non-solicit at all), which would be disproportionate given the clause is mutual and otherwise narrow. Instead, § 2 creates an evergreen term that continues until terminated under § 6, and § 6(a) lets either party — including us — terminate for any or no reason on fifteen (15) days' notice whenever no Statement of Work is outstanding. That structure is at least as favourable to us as the preferred position (no automatic renewal, exit on well under 30 days' notice, no committed multi-year renewal, no unilateral price escalation), so there is nothing to redline. Noted only for completeness: because there is no renewal pricing mechanic, fee changes would need to be agreed in each Statement of Work; if we later add renewal terms we should carry in the CPI/3% uplift cap.","verification":"skipped"},{"id":"f-transition-a266f440","ruleId":"TRANSITION","ruleTitle":"Post-termination transition assistance and data return","severity":"medium","status":"missing","sectionRef":"§ 6 TERMINATION.","rationale":"Section 6 (and the duplicate termination text at p0044) addresses only final payment and assignment of Works in progress; it says nothing about transition assistance, return of Company data or deletion/certification. No usable clause exists anywhere in the Agreement, so the rule is missing. There is no warranty that the Services or Works will conform to the Specifications or documentation, no warranty duration, and no repair/re-perform/refund remedy; Section 1(b) contains only a general workmanlike performance covenant, and Section 4, despite its \"ACCEPTANCE\" heading, contains no acceptance or rejection mechanic that could serve as a practical remedy. The clause therefore fails even the fallback (90 days software / 30 days services with remedies). The disclaimer in 5(e) preserves express warranties, so no carve-out is needed; we added a 90-day conformity warranty with a re-performance, repair or refund remedy and renumbered the disclaimer.","proposal":"Add express conformity-to-Specifications warranty (90 days) with repair/re-perform/refund remedy","verification":"skipped"},{"id":"f-insurance-982d8a99","ruleId":"INSURANCE","ruleTitle":"Vendor insurance","severity":"low","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 7 LIMITATIONS OF LIABILITY; INDEMNIFICATION OF CONTRACTOR.","rationale":"Contrary to the planner's assumption, an insurance covenant does exist at § 7 ¶ 14 (p0048). It carries workers' compensation as required by statute, CGL of USD 1,000,000, E&O of USD 1,000,000, and certificates/evidence of insurance on Company request with notice of material change — so the general liability, workers' comp and certificate elements are satisfied, and E&O sits at the playbook fallback level (USD 1M rather than the preferred USD 2M), which we note but do not redline. The material gap is cyber/privacy liability, which the fallback requires at USD 2,000,000. Contractor plainly touches our data: Confidential Information is defined at p0038 as documents, software, reports, data and records obtained by Contractor from Company in performing Services, and p0007 contemplates Contractor personnel working at Company facilities and accessing Company computer systems. With no cyber coverage at all for a vendor that handles our data and systems, the clause fails the fallback on that term. Minimal fix: insert cyber liability (network security and privacy) coverage of USD 5,000,000, scoped to where Contractor processes Company data, leaving the remaining coverages and the existing certificate mechanic untouched; USD 2,000,000 is offered as the fallback in the comment.","proposal":"Add cyber/privacy liability coverage to the existing insurance covenant, since Contractor handles Company data and accesses Company systems.","verification":"skipped"}]

{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — RadialSpark Consulting Services Agreement

**To:** Deal Team / Business Sponsor  
**From:** In-house Counsel (Customer side — Clear Capital)  
**Re:** Playbook review of the Consulting Services Agreement with RadialSpark ("Contractor")  
**Privileged & Confidential — Attorney-Client Communication**

---

## 1. Executive Summary

We have completed our playbook review of the Agreement. Of the eighteen rules assessed, ten are compliant and require no action, six are deviations requiring redlines, and two rules are unaddressed by the document entirely.

The commercial architecture of the deal is broadly favourable to us. There is no exclusivity, no non-compete, no minimum purchase or take-or-pay commitment, no most-favoured-nation obligation, no liquidated damages or early-termination fee, no auto-renewal (the term is evergreen and exitable), and no audit right exercisable against us. Ownership of deliverables sits substantially at our preferred position — Works vest in Clear Capital with an assignment of works-in-progress on termination — and the residual licence-back of Contractor pre-existing materials is royalty-free, perpetual and sublicensable.

Our concerns concentrate in the ri[REDACTED] provisions. Three items are, on our playbook, walk-away issues: (i) there is **no Vendor indemnity whatsoever** — Section 7 is captioned "Indemnification of Contractor" but contains only a cap, a consequential-damages waiver and a fees waiver, and the cap's sole carve-out cross-refers to Paragraph 9 (Independent Contractor), confirming the indemnity was never drafted in; (ii) the **liability cap** is measured per Statement of Work against fees actually paid, with no floor and no carve-outs for confidentiality, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, indemnity or IP infringement; and (iii) we have **no termination-for-convenience right** while any Statement of Work is outstanding, which on an evergreen, SOW-driven engagement means no practical exit.

Secondary deviations are more readily resolved: Arizona governing law (outside our accepted list) with no venue clause at all; no assignment carve-out for our affiliates or successors; no conformity warranty, duration or remedy; no post-termination transition or data return/deletion obligation; a mutual non-solicit lacking a general-advertising carve-out; and an otherwise sound insurance covenant with no cyber/privacy coverage despite Contractor handling our data and accessing our systems.

We recommend proceeding on the basis of the attached redlines, treating the indemnity, cap carve-outs and convenience-termination right as conditions of signature.

---

## 2. Findings Table

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | **Missing** | § 7 (Limitations of Liability; Indemnification of Contractor) | No operative indemnity language anywhere; heading only. Walk-away territory. Inserting Contractor indemnity as new § 7(d) with claim mechanics and carve-out from § 7 limitations. |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | § 4 (Ownership of Materials; Acceptance) | Works vest in Clear Capital; assignment of works-in-progress on termination; perpetual sublicensable licence-back. Substantially preferred position. Not redlined. |
| 3 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | **Deviation** | § 7 | Mutual, but cap measured per SOW on fees actually paid with no floor; only carve-out cross-refers to § 9 (Independent Contractor). Fails fallback. |
| 4 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | **Deviation** | § 7 / § 10 | Symmetrical consent standard, but no affiliate/successor carve-out for Company; fails fallback. No change-of-control trigger (acceptable). |
| 5 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | § 1 (Purpose of Engagement) | Task-by-task engagement via SOWs; no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation. Preferred position. |
| 6 | High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties on Customer | Compliant | § 6 (Termination) | No liquidated damages, penalty, minimum fee or early-termination fee. Only accrued fees on termination. Preferred position. |
| 7 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | § 4 | Royalty-free, non-exclusive, perpetual, sublicensable; no revocation right; broad business-operations scope. Meets material terms. |
| 8 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | § 4 | No non-compete, exclusivity or field-of-use restriction on Clear Capital. Preferred position. |
| 9 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Deviation** | § 6 | Convenience right available only when no SOW is outstanding; evergreen term. Fails preferred and fallback; walk-away territory. |
| 10 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 3 (Contractor's Compensation) | No audit, inspection or verification right against us. At or above preferred by default. |
| 11 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | **Deviation** | § 7 / § 11 | Arizona law, outside accepted list (NY, DE, CA, England & Wales); no forum or venue provision at all. |
| 12 | Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation on Customer | Compliant | § 3 | No parity, price-matching or best-terms obligation. Preferred position. |
| 13 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments / volume restrictions | Compliant | § 3 | Time-and-materials, task-by-task; no committed spend, shortfall or lock-in. Preferred position. |
| 14 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | **Deviation** | § 7 / § 13 | Mutual, 12 months, narrow — but no general-advertising or unsolicited-approach carve-out, which the fallback requires. |
| 15 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Compliant | § 1 / § 2 | No auto-renewal; evergreen term exitable on 15 days' notice when no SOW outstanding. At least as favourable as preferred. |
| 16 | Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | **Missing** | § 6 | No transition assistance, data return, deletion or certification anywhere; confidentiality clause imposes no return-or-destroy duty. |
| 17 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | **Deviation** | § 5 (Representations and Warranties; Disclaimer) | No conformity warranty, no duration, no repair/re-perform/refund remedy; no acceptance mechanic despite § 4 heading. Fails fallback. |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | **Deviation** | § 7 / ¶ 14 | Workers' comp, CGL USD 1M, E&O USD 1M and certificates present (E&O at fallback). No cyber/privacy coverage despite data and system access. |

---

## 3. Walk-Away Items

The following three findings sit in walk-away territory on our playbook and should be treated as conditions of signature rather than negotiating preferences.

**3.1 No Vendor indemnity (§ 7 — INDEMN, critical, missing).** The Agreement contains no indemnity of any kind. Section 5 gives an unqualified non-infringement warranty but no defence or indemnity obligation, and the cap's only carve-out points to the Independent Contractor clause. We are asking for a Contractor indemnity as new § 7(d) covering third-party IP infringement, breach of law, unauthorised access to Company data, and gross negligence or wilful misconduct, with standard notice, control and cooperation mechanics and an express carve-out from the § 7 limitations so the indemnity is not neutralised by the cap or the fees waiver. No Customer indemnity exists, so no reciprocal narrowing is required.

**3.2 Liability cap fails the fallback on two material terms (§ 7 — LOL-CAP, critical, deviation).** Mutuality is satisfied, but Contractor's cap is measured per Statement of Work against fees actually paid for those particular Services — which on a time-and-materials engagement can fall well below twelve months' fees — with no USD floor, and there are no carve-outs for confidentiality, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, indemnification or infringement of Company IP.
